title: Project 42 Daily AI Work Quick Reference
summary: Use a compact orient, plan, execute, verify, and recover loop for everyday AI-assisted work, with deeper Project 42 guides for specialized decisions.
prerequisites: An authorized task and target workspace
A way to review changes and observable results

sections.title: Orient and plan
paragraphs: Confirm the requested outcome, target, owner, repository or system instructions, current state, protected data, allowed actions, and stop conditions. Separate facts from assumptions and identify the smallest evidence that will prove success.

Use AI Coding Workspace Bootstrap for first-time setup, Agent Configuration Layering Reference for conflicting settings, and the relevant coding-tool operating card when choosing permissions and interaction style.

Observed evidence is what you can directly inspect, such as the supplied ticket rows, a displayed branch name, or a reviewed diff. An assumption is something not established by the inputs, such as whether the sample represents all tickets or whether a local file is unchanged. Label assumptions rather than presenting them as facts.

Treat names, email addresses, account identifiers, payment details, authentication material, health information, and other identifying or sensitive content as protected data. Do not paste it into a model unless the task, authorization, and handling rules explicitly permit it. Prefer synthetic or redacted inputs.

code.label: Daily task card
code.code:
Task: Analyze the six supplied synthetic support tickets and recommend one triage priority; separately prepare a proposed local documentation change for docs/triage.md without applying it.
Scope: Read only the supplied ticket table and the local file docs/triage.md; analyze the six rows; propose only the bounded checklist addition described below; exclude all other files, tickets, repositories, deployments, network calls, and external writes.
Permissions: Read the supplied text and the named local file; write nothing; run no commands; use no network, tools, credentials, or external actions.
Known state: The ticket table is synthetic and complete for this exercise; the local file's actual contents, branch, version, and status are not supplied and must not be claimed as observed.
Evidence needed: A row-by-row count, arithmetic that totals six, a recommendation with uncertainty, the proposed text or diff for docs/triage.md, and a list of limits and assumptions.
Stop conditions: Any request to use real protected data, inspect an unlisted path, alter unrelated content, run a command, use a credential or network, make an external write, or infer a fact not supported by the supplied inputs.
Verification: Recount every supplied row; check category and status totals against six; review the proposed change against the exact scope; confirm no external action was taken; state unresolved uncertainty.
Recovery: Stop, preserve the supplied evidence and draft, identify whether any write occurred, restore the last verified state if an authorized write occurred, rerun only the smallest deterministic check, and report what remains unverified.

sections.title: Execute in small observable steps
paragraphs: Inspect before editing, make the smallest coherent change, and keep unrelated user work intact. Review every new dependency, file, command, network call, permission expansion, and external write. Capture useful outputs and stable identifiers without secrets or unnecessary personal data.
Use Commands, Hooks, and Automation Guide before turning a repeated step into executable automation. Use the MCP trust and tool-contract guides before attaching new tools or servers.

A confident answer is not evidence by itself. Check totals from the complete input, ask for the rows used, and compare the answer with independently repeatable arithmetic. If a model reports a result that cannot be reproduced from the supplied inputs, mark it unverified.

GitHub's About Git guide is a reference for Git concepts, but this quick reference does not require Git or any particular provider. A local or offline model can follow the same bounded review and verification process. Source: https://docs.github.com/en/get-started/using-git/about-git.

code.label: Reusable analysis prompt
code.code:
You are analyzing a small synthetic support-ticket table. Do not invent rows, fields, causes, severity, customer identity, or business impact. Return exactly these headings: ROW CHECK, STATUS COUNTS, CATEGORY COUNTS, RECOMMENDATION, UNCERTAINTY, PROTECTED DATA.

Input rows:
T-101 | category=login access | status=resolved
T-102 | category=billing duplicate charge | status=open
T-103 | category=login access | status=resolved
T-104 | category=shipping delay | status=resolved
T-105 | category=billing duplicate charge | status=escalated
T-106 | category=login access | status=resolved

Required checks:
1. List all six ticket IDs exactly once.
2. Show status counts and category counts.
3. Show arithmetic proving each set of counts totals 6.
4. Recommend one priority using only the observed rows.
5. State at least two uncertainties caused by missing fields.
6. State that the rows contain no names, email addresses, account numbers, or payment details, and advise against adding such data.
7. Do not claim that a ticket was actually fixed, escalated, contacted, or deployed.

sections.title: Worked example: support-ticket analysis
paragraphs: This is a complete synthetic example, not an observation from a real support system. The observed evidence is exactly the six rows below. Assumptions are limited to treating the supplied six rows as the complete dataset for this exercise. There is no supplied severity, age, service-level target, customer impact, owner, resolution quality, or causal information.

Every row: T-101, category login access, status resolved. T-102, category billing duplicate charge, status open. T-103, category login access, status resolved. T-104, category shipping delay, status resolved. T-105, category billing duplicate charge, status escalated. T-106, category login access, status resolved.

Observed status counts: resolved=4, open=1, escalated=1. Check: 4+1+1=6. Observed category counts: login access=3, billing duplicate charge=2, shipping delay=1. Check: 3+2+1=6. The six distinct IDs are T-101, T-102, T-103, T-104, T-105, and T-106, so the row count also equals 6.

Recommendation: prioritize the billing duplicate charge category for review because it has two of the six supplied tickets, and both observed billing tickets are not marked resolved: one is open and one is escalated. This is a triage recommendation from frequency and status only. It is not proof that billing causes more harm or that either ticket is more urgent than a login or shipping ticket.

Uncertainty: the sample is small and synthetic; it may not represent the wider queue. Missing severity, ticket age, customer impact, service-level target, and resolution details prevent a stronger priority claim. The dataset does not establish why any issue occurred or whether any customer received a satisfactory outcome.

Protected-data check: the supplied rows contain ticket IDs, categories, and statuses only. They do not contain names, email addresses, account numbers, payment details, or authentication material. Do not add those details merely to make the analysis seem more realistic. The NIST AI Risk Management Framework is a relevant source for organizing AI risk management considerations: https://www.nist.gov/itl/ai-risk-management-framework.

code.label: Independently checkable arithmetic
code.code:
Rows = 6
Status total = resolved 4 + open 1 + escalated 1 = 6
Category total = login access 3 + billing duplicate charge 2 + shipping delay 1 = 6
Billing unresolved rows = T-102 open + T-105 escalated = 2

sections.title: Worked example: bounded local documentation change handoff
paragraphs: This is an explicitly fictional, self-contained documentation fixture. It is not a real repository observation. The supplied before-state below is the complete fictional content of docs/triage.md. The requested result is a proposal only: prepare the smallest patch that adds one heading and exactly three checklist lines while preserving every unrelated line.

The allowed target is only docs/triage.md. The fixture provides the before text and the exact proposed after text, so a learner can review the proposal without executing commands or accessing a filesystem. In a real workspace, an authorized operator would still need to inspect the actual file before applying anything. If the actual file differs from this fixture, the section already exists, or unrelated edits are present, stop and request review.

The proposal does not authorize a filesystem edit, commit, push, deployment, publication, network request, credential use, or other external action. The completed record below reports only evidence supplied in this fictional exercise. It does not claim that a real file was read or changed.

Review the complete before and proposed-after text, then compare the diff. A beginner should verify that the target is one file, that the heading and three checklist lines match exactly, and that all unrelated text is unchanged. Reject the patch if it changes any existing line, adds another file, changes whitespace outside the proposed addition, or places the new section in a different location without approval. A reviewed proposal does not imply deployment because review establishes only that the text is acceptable on paper. There is no evidence here of a filesystem write, commit, push, deployment, publication, or user-facing availability.

sections.title: Learner exercise: changed input
paragraphs: Use the prompt below with any provider, including a local model. The input changes two statuses from the worked example: T-102 is now resolved instead of open, and T-104 is now open instead of resolved. Do not use the worked-example counts as a shortcut.

Deterministic expected results: list six distinct IDs. Status counts must be resolved=4, open=1, escalated=1, with 4+1+1=6. Category counts must remain login access=3, billing duplicate charge=2, shipping delay=1, with 3+2+1=6. The billing category has one unresolved row, T-105, while the shipping category has one unresolved row, T-104. A defensible recommendation is billing duplicate charge because it still has two rows and includes the only escalated row, but the recommendation remains uncertain because severity, age, impact, and service-level information are absent.

Exact learner answer: ROW CHECK: T-101, T-102, T-103, T-104, T-105, T-106, each once. STATUS COUNTS: resolved=4, open=1, escalated=1; total 4+1+1=6. CATEGORY COUNTS: login access=3, billing duplicate charge=2, shipping delay=1; total 3+2+1=6. RECOMMENDATION: prioritize billing duplicate charge for review because it has two rows and includes T-105, the only escalated row. UNCERTAINTY: the six-row synthetic sample lacks severity, age, customer impact, service-level target, and causal or resolution evidence. PROTECTED DATA: no names, email addresses, account numbers, or payment details are supplied; do not add them.

Rationale: changing two rows does not change the overall status totals because one row moved into resolved while another moved out of resolved. Category totals do not change because the category fields stayed the same. The recommendation follows the observed count and escalation marker, not an invented claim about harm or urgency.

sections.title: Expected result and verification
paragraphs: Closeout for the fictional documentation fixture: the requested outcome was to prepare, but not apply, a bounded addition to docs/triage.md. The supplied evidence is sufficient to review the proposal textually. It is not evidence about any real filesystem, repository, branch, deployment, publication, or user-facing result.

A beginner can verify the proposal by checking that the before-state contains one complete file, that the proposed after-state contains the same existing text plus the requested heading and three exact checklist lines, and that the diff names only docs/triage.md. Check the hunk manually: no existing line has a minus sign, and the only added content is the blank separator, the heading, and the three checklist lines. Reject the patch if any unrelated text changes, if another file appears, if the heading or checklist wording differs, or if the target's actual context does not match the supplied fixture.

The reviewed proposal does not imply deployment. A proposal and review show intended content and scope only. Deployment or user-facing availability would require separate evidence such as an authorized filesystem result, an applicable check result, a commit or other recorded change, and evidence of the relevant publication or release postcondition. None of those actions or results is supplied here.

The original verification and recovery rule still applies: a successful command is not enough when the user-facing or external postcondition remains unverified. When a result is wrong or uncertain, stop before another consequential action, preserve redacted evidence, determine whether any external write occurred, restore the last verified state or apply approved compensation, rerun the smallest deterministic check, and report what remains unverified.
